newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels say not attending next round of talks.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels say not attending next round of talks.

text.p: Marxist rebels holding 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima said on Thursday they would not attend the next round of negotiations with the government scheduled for Friday.

"Tomorrow we are not going to attend the negotiations," Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini said in a walkie-talkie conversation from inside the residence. He said he did not know when talks would restart.

Cerpa said the rebels had decided not to attend what would have been the tenth round of talks because they feared the government might be planning an attack on the diplomatic mansion in their absence.
"All of a sudden they are waiting for us to leave to start an attack, taking advantage of our absence," Cerpa told Reuters.
Cerpa said that the talks were suspended until the security situation "was cleared up." He said he would meet with the talks guarantors to express his concerns over a possible attack.
Cerpa's announcement marked the first time a round has been called off since negotiations started Feb. 11 at a Red Cross safe house.
